criterion: The feature atlas on the homepage and the pricing board on the paid route are hairline grids, where a one-pixel gap over a border-coloured ground is the only rule between neighbouring cells.
evaluation_rule: The feature atlas is the eight-cell block of four across and two down on the homepage; the pricing board is the plan block on /plus. Yes when each cell of both blocks is painted with the card ground, when the lines between cells are gaps of about one pixel showing a paler ground behind, when no cell carries a border of a different colour from those gaps, and when the gaps run edge to edge without breaking at a cell corner. No when the divisions are drawn borders that double up between neighbouring cells, when a gap shows the page ground rather than a paler border ground, when the cells carry a radius, or when either block is laid out as separate bordered cards with space between.

criterion: Every label, kicker, numeral, badge, code fragment and control across the homepage, the gallery and the pricing board is set in the mono family, and nothing read as a sentence is.
evaluation_rule: Yes when the navigation labels, the two-digit section indexes, the category count badges, the filter row, the price banner, the mono uppercase kickers above each band, the source panel and every button label render in a monospaced face, and when the hero title, the feature blurbs, the category blurbs, the article standfirsts and the body prose render in a proportional face. No when a navigation label or a count badge renders in the proportional face, when a feature blurb or a category blurb renders in the monospaced face, when one face carries the whole page, or when the two faces are the same family at different weights.

criterion: One header ships on every route, sitting on the accent ground with the brand lockup at the left, five navigation labels, and the paid action at the right.
evaluation_rule: Yes when exactly one header treatment appears across the root, /docs, /examples, /ui, /plus, /changelog and /@nova, when the header is inset from each side and sticks to the top of the viewport while the page scrolls under, when the ground of the header is the route accent with dark ink on top, when the brand lockup sits at the left, when the labels read Docs, Examples, UI, Magazine and the paid action, and when hovering a label rolls a second identical copy of the same word up into place. No when the reading routes carry a different header treatment from the product routes, when the header scrolls away, when the ground is the page ground rather than the accent, when a label is missing, or when hovering a label changes the word rather than rolling an identical copy.

criterion: Choosing a facet in the gallery filter row changes the address, and the grid that comes back is the server's answer for the new address rather than a reordering of the previous grid.
evaluation_rule: The filter row is the mono uppercase control row above the gallery grid on /examples. Yes when choosing the runtime react puts a runtime term in the address, when choosing the category hero-sections adds a category term beside the runtime term, when the count line above the grid falls to the number of examples matching both, when opening the narrowed address a second time produces the same cards in the same order, and when the grid arrives with the document rather than appearing after a separate fetch. No when narrowing leaves the address unchanged, when the count line keeps the unnarrowed number, when opening the narrowed address a second time produces a different order, or when the grid is empty in the served document and filled in afterwards.

criterion: The purchase panel opens over the pricing board leaving the route in place, and after a completed purchase the board states that the member holds the licence rather than offering the purchase again.
evaluation_rule: The pricing board is the plan block on /plus and the purchase panel is the overlay the plan action opens. Yes when the panel opens over the board with the board still visible behind, when the panel collects a display name and an email address, when submitting produces a confirmation naming the licence key and the total amount, when closing the panel returns to /plus rather than to another route, and when the board then states that the licence is already held. No when the plan action navigates away from /plus, when the board vanishes behind an opaque page, when the confirmation names neither the licence key nor the amount, or when the board still offers the purchase to a member who has just completed one.

criterion: The save control on a gallery card fills the moment the control is pressed and then settles against the server's answer, and a refused save returns the control to the previous state and states the reason on the card.
evaluation_rule: The save control is the heart at the right of a card's meta bar. Yes when pressing the control fills the heart in the accent before the answer arrives, when a successful save leaves the heart filled after a reload, when a save refused by the server returns the heart to the outline state, when the reason for a refusal appears on that card rather than in a banner elsewhere on the page, and when pressing the control with no session takes the visitor to sign in rather than failing quietly. No when the heart waits for the answer before filling, when a refused save leaves the heart filled, when the reason appears far from the card, or when pressing the control with no session does nothing visible.

criterion: A gallery card states whether the source behind the card can be opened, legibly from the grid alone.
evaluation_rule: Yes when a free example's card carries no lock mark and an open action reading as an ordinary open, when a paid example's card seen without the licence carries a lock mark in the meta bar and an open action reading as an upgrade, when a paid example's card seen with the licence is indistinguishable from a free one, when a saved card's heart is filled in the accent, and when the thumbnail plays on hover in all four states. No when a locked card looks the same as a free one, when the lock mark sits outside the meta bar, when a card held by a licensed reader still reads as an upgrade, or when the locked card's thumbnail refuses to play.

criterion: Every gallery, preview well and saved panel that can be empty, unstarted or refused says which, and a refusal that came from a failure to resolve the licence reads apart from an offer to buy.
evaluation_rule: Yes when a facet combination matching nothing shows a stated empty grid with a control to clear the facets rather than a blank column, when a preview well that has not started holds the size the media will take, when a preview that did not start says as much while the rest of the page stays usable, when an entitlement that could not be resolved says the licence could not be confirmed and invites another attempt, when an example never bought instead offers the purchase, and when a member's own empty saved panel keeps a heading and an empty state. No when an empty grid looks like a page that failed to load, when a preview well collapses to nothing before starting, when an unresolved licence and a never-bought example produce the same page, or when an empty saved panel disappears.

criterion: Cards, buttons, inputs, thumbnails and panels meet their corners square, and one diagonal hatch at a single odd angle is stamped behind the primary action, the reading-route headers, the account frame, the catalogue thumbnails and the changelog version plate.
evaluation_rule: Yes when the gallery cards, the category cards, the plan blocks, the filter controls, the account fields and the source panels all meet their corners square, when the few rounded shapes on the site are limited to dots, pills, terminal chrome and a tab strip, when a repeating diagonal stripe at a single angle steeper than forty-five degrees sits behind the primary action, the dossier header on a reading route, the account form frame, the gallery thumbnails and the changelog version plate, and when that angle is the same in all five places. No when cards or buttons carry a radius, when the hatch angle differs between two of the five places, when the hatch is a flat wash with no visible stripe, or when no hatch appears at all.

criterion: The page ground is a near-black carrying a trace of green under a warm off-white ink, and the accent comes from one attribute on the root element, resolving to amber on the library routes and to green on the paid, account and profile routes.
evaluation_rule: Yes when the ground behind every product route is a very dark green-tinted near-black, when body ink is a warm off-white rather than pure white, when secondary ink is a neutral warm grey, when a card sits one step lighter than the ground, when the accent on the root, /docs, /examples and /ui is an amber yellow, when the accent on /plus, /login and /@nova is a green, and when one attribute on the root element is what changes between the two. No when the ground is a neutral black or a grey, when the ink is pure white, when a route mixes both accents at once, when the paid route is amber, or when the accent appears to be written into each component rather than read from the root.

criterion: Hovering the primary action sends a diagonal edge across the button at the slant of the wordmark bars, with both label copies inverting at the moment the edge passes, and the hero title wipes in from the left once on load.
evaluation_rule: Yes when the fill on the primary action arrives as a slanted edge travelling from left to right rather than as a fade or a slide, when the slant matches the slant of the bars in the wordmark, when the label ink inverts as the edge reaches the label rather than before or after, when the label is never caught half inverted, when the hero title on the root is revealed once on load by a clip opening from the left, and when no effect anywhere under the pointer runs longer than about half a second. No when the action fades or slides instead of wiping, when the slant differs from the wordmark, when the label inverts before the edge arrives, when the hero title is fully open from the first frame, or when a hover effect runs for a second or more.

criterion: Every interactive element in the header, the gallery filter row and the sign-in form carries a visible focus indicator that differs from the hover treatment, every field carries a real label element, and the result of a save is announced politely.
evaluation_rule: Yes when moving the keyboard onto the navigation labels, the filter row, a card's save control, the account fields and the plan action shows an outline on each that is not the hover treatment, when the wipe on the primary action is never the only focus indicator, when the account fields and the newsletter field each have a label element rather than a placeholder standing in for one, when a drawn figure carries a text alternative describing what the figure demonstrates, when the keyboard can enter and leave the framed preview, and when the outcome of pressing a save control is announced without stealing focus. No when focus and hover look identical, when a field's only label is a placeholder, when the keyboard cannot leave the framed preview, or when a drawn figure has no alternative text at all.

criterion: The layout changes at four width thresholds, the pricing board stacking at the third of them, and the navigation labels switch to their short forms at the narrowest with every control still present.
evaluation_rule: Yes when a viewport just under 1200px keeps the content column following the viewport with narrower gutters, when a viewport just under 900px stacks the two-column bands and halves the feature atlas columns, when a viewport just under 760px stacks the pricing board and reduces the comparison table to one column, when a viewport at about 390px shows the short navigation labels, full-width stacked hero actions and a halved footer column set, when no control present on the widest layout is missing from the narrowest, and when no route scrolls sideways at 390px. No when the layout jumps at widths other than those four, when a control disappears rather than moving at a narrow width, when the navigation labels stay long at 390px, or when any route overflows sideways.
